title: Audit, price and win your first analytics clients

say: Audit, price and win your first analytics clients.
This is the video for Module 3 of Marketing Analytics and Reporting.
Before you build anything for a client, find out what she must decide and whether her data can be trusted. That is discovery and the audit. Then you price the work fairly.

panel.heading: What you will be able to do
items: Run discovery and a ten-point audit
Price a setup fee plus a monthly retainer
Write a scope that protects your hours
Build proof and a 90-day plan

say: You also write a clear scope, build portfolio proof, and plan your first 90 days. Shops, service firms, agencies, NGOs and remote clients all need this work.

say: Never ask for a client's passwords. In GA4, Meta and Google Ads, the owner can add you by email with a limited role. A Viewer or Analyst role is enough for reporting.

panel.heading: Handle client access and data safely

cards.d: Ask the owner to add you as a user. Request the lowest role that does the job.
Ask for sales exports without names, phone numbers or addresses.
Keep client files in a password-protected account. Delete them when the work ends.

say: Ask for sales exports with customer names, phone numbers and addresses removed, unless you truly need them.

panel.heading: Handle client access and data safely

say: Keep files off shared family phones, and delete them at the end. Nigeria's Data Protection Act 2023 gives people rights over their data. Treat every customer list as a trust.

say: For example, Kemi runs a catering company in Abuja. Discovery starts with her decision. She wants to know if Google search is worth continuing, because enquiries feel low quality.

panel.heading: Kemi's measurement audit
items: Discovery: is Google search worth it?
Audit score: 6 of 10 checks, 60%
Form key event fires twice
No UTM rules, WhatsApp source not recorded
Rank the fixes, write a one-page summary

say: The ten-point audit passes 6 of 10 checks. The big problem: her form key event fires twice per enquiry. So Google Ads has been told it gets twice the real leads, and its cost per lead looks half of what it is.

say: There are no UTM rules, and WhatsApp enquiries have no source. So she adds a how did you hear about us column.

say: Rank every fix by impact and effort. Clients rarely understand tags, but they understand: your dashboard has been counting every enquiry twice.

say: Analytics work is heavy at the start, then lighter each month. So price it as a setup fee plus a monthly retainer. Your rate is your own decision. These are practice numbers, not market rates.

card.title: Zainab prices her work
card.note: Practice figures, not market rates. Approximate.

say: Zainab estimates 28 setup hours. At 8,000 naira, that is 224,000. She adds 15% for surprises and rounds to 260,000 naira. She asks for 50% before work starts.

card.title: Zainab prices her work
card.note: Practice figures, not market rates. Approximate.

say: Each month takes 8 hours, so 65,000 naira. That is 10% of her client's 650,000 naira ad spend. If her reports cut wasted spend by even 10%, the fee pays for itself.

card.title: Zainab prices her work

say: A clear scope protects you. Name the data sources, deliverables and dates, revisions, exclusions, the client's duties, and a change-request rule.
Can you just quickly check why sales dropped last Tuesday? That is how unpaid hours begin. Answer kindly, estimate the hours, and agree in writing first, even on WhatsApp.

panel.heading: Write these into every scope
items: Data sources included
Deliverables and dates
Up to two rounds of revisions
Exclusions, such as running ads
Client duties, such as access
Change requests quoted in writing

say: You do not need a client to start. Google's free GA4 demo account has real but disguised data from an online store, for practice reports.

panel.heading: A case study that persuades
items: Situation: the business and its decision
What you did: audit, fixes, report
What you found: checked insights
What changed: action and result
Artefacts: blurred report screenshot

say: Write each case study in five parts: situation, what you did, what you found, what changed, and the artefacts.
Always ask permission before showing client work. An honestly labelled practice case study is better than an inflated real one.

say: For example, Chidinma manages social media in Enugu. In her first four weeks she earns the Google Analytics Certification, builds a demo report and writes a case study.

panel.heading: Chidinma runs her plan like a funnel
items: Weeks 1 to 4: certificate, demo report, case study
Weeks 5 to 12: 5 contacts a week, 60 in total
1 in 10 books a call: 6 calls
1 in 3 calls buys an audit: 2 clients

say: Then she contacts 5 suitable businesses a week, offering a fixed-price audit. That is 60 contacts. If 1 in 10 books a call, and 1 in 3 calls buys, she wins 2 clients by day 90.

panel.heading: Chidinma runs her plan like a funnel

1 in 10 books a call: 6 calls

say: These rates are her own guesses. On day 90 she replaces them with real numbers. Keep messages short and specific, and never send bulk unsolicited messages.

panel.rule: Log your numbers every Friday and compare with your guesses.

say: To remember. Never ask for passwords, and protect customer data. Audit the data before you report on it. Price setup and retainer from honest hours.
Agree scope in writing, and take a deposit before setup work starts.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Never ask for passwords

Setup fee plus monthly retainer
Scope in writing, deposit first
Honest, permitted case studies
